articles.title: La combinada de la Champions- Jueves 09/09
articles.standfirst: 1XBET te ofrece la apuesta combinada de la primera jornada de la Champions 26/27, correspondiente a los encuentros del jueves 9 de septiembre
articles.summary: 1XBET te ofrece la apuesta combinada de la primera jornada de la Champions 26/27, correspondiente a los encuentros del jueves 9 de septiembre
articles.body: La Champions League 26/27 continúa este jueves con seis nuevos debuts. El Fenerbahçe recibe a la Roma a las 18:45. A la misma hora se disputa el Bayern Múnich-Bodo/Glimt, el PSV Eindhoven-Shakhtar Donetsk y el Como-Leipzig. Más tarde, a las 21:00, llegan el Manchester United-Sabah y el Slavia Praga-Lens. Pronóstico 1: Más de 2.5 goles El mercado de goles totales aparece como una de las alternativas más interesantes del encuentro. El Fenerbahçe ha marcado en sus últimos 15 partidos consecutivos y no pierde en casa desde hace 11 encuentros, mientras que la Roma llega como líder invicta de la Serie A. Su último precedente europeo, un vibrante 3-3, deja claro que entre ambos el arco no suele descansar. 1XBET paga el +2.5 goles totales a 1.74. Pronóstico 2: Más de 4.5 goles El conjunto de Vincent Kompany llega de encadenar seis victorias consecutivas en todas las competiciones, aunque el pasado fin de semana no pudo pasar del empate sin goles ante el recién ascendido Schalke. El Bodo/Glimt, por su parte, es un rival nada sencillo. Acumula 17 partidos sin perder y llega tras eliminar con autoridad al NEC Nijmegen en la previa. 1XBET sitúa la cuota del +4.5 goles totales en 1.85. Pronóstico 3: Ambos equipos marcan Dos equipos de perfil ofensivo protagonizan este cruce, habituales en anotar en la mayoría de sus partidos tanto en competición doméstica como en Europa. El Shakhtar, pese a jugar sus partidos como local fuera de Ucrania, ha mostrado en los últimos años una gran capacidad para hacer daño arriba incluso ante rivales de mayor entidad. 1XBET paga a 1.58 que ambos equipos marquen. Pronóstico 4: Más de 2.5 goles El conjunto italiano, en su primera participación europea en décadas, afronta este debut con ambición ofensiva bajo la batuta de Cesc Fàbregas. El Leipzig, por su parte, es un habitual de la Champions League en los últimos años y suele marcar con facilidad incluso lejos de Alemania. 1XBET paga el +2.5 goles totales a 1.57. Pronóstico 5: Gana el Manchester United al descanso Los Red Devils regresan a la Champions League tras varias temporadas de ausencia, y lo hacen en Old Trafford ante un rival debutante absoluto en la fase liga. El Sabah, campeón de Azerbaiyán, ha hecho méritos en la previa con goleadas como el 5-0 sobre el Zira, pero la diferencia de nivel respecto al United, con Mbeumo, Bruno Fernandes y Rashford como principales referencias, resulta demasiado amplia. 1XBET paga la victoria local al descanso a 1.46. Pronóstico 6: Ambos equipos marcan El conjunto checo, habitual ya de las últimas ediciones de la Champions League, suele mostrarse un rival incómodo en campo propio y con capacidad para generar peligro ante cualquier rival. El Lens, por su parte, llega de protagonizar partidos con goles en las últimas jornadas de la Ligue 1, lo que invita a pensar en un duelo abierto por los dos lados. 1XBET paga esta opción a 1.59. La combinada propuesta para esta jornada de la Champions reúne que ambos equipos anoten en el Slavia de Praga vs Lens (1.59) y PSV Eindhoven vs Shakhtar Donetsk (1.58) , el +2.5 goles totales del Fenerbahçe vs Roma (1.74) y Como vs Leipzig (1.57), el +4.5 goles en el Bayern vs Bodo (1.85) y el triunfo del Manchester United al descanso (1.46). La cuota combinada asciende hasta 18.53, fruto de la multiplicación de las seis cuotas. Una propuesta para quienes buscan comenzar la temporada con una selección de mercados atractivos entre las casas de apuestas online, de la mano de 1XBET.

articles.title: Atlético, un traspié para repetir el camino
articles.standfirst: Aunque lamenta no haber sabido conservar el quinto gol de Llorente en Anfield, toma como espejo la trayectoria que condujo a las semifinales
articles.summary: Aunque lamenta no haber sabido conservar el quinto gol de Llorente en Anfield, toma como espejo la trayectoria que condujo a las semifinales
articles.body: Como si se tratara del día de la marmota, empieza a ser demasiado previsible que no hay visita de Llorente a Anfield sin gol. Sin embargo, para amargura del Atlético, también empieza a repetirse que los inicios en la Champions sean duros. Así, como ocurrió la campaña pasada, el idilio de Marcos con el mítico estadio no sirvió para volver con algún punto. No obstante, en la expedición rojiblanca también se sabe que lo importante no es cómo se empieza, sino cómo se acaba. No hay que remontarse demasiado. La campaña pasada, pese al 3-2 final en el estreno en Anfield (aunque el doblete de Llorente llegó a servir para igualar el partido, un gol de Van Dijk en la prolongación caería como un jarro de agua fría), el Atlético acabaría disputando las semifinales frente al Arsenal. Del mismo modo que el ejercicio anterior, pese al triunfo frente al Leipzig para arrancar, la primera salida también implicaría un revolcón, el 4-0 frente al Benfica. Una derrota que no impediría que el Atlético acabara entrando en el ‘top 8’, justo antes de verse apeado de la competición por el polémico doble toque del penalti de Julián Alvarez. De ahí que, más allá de lamentar no haber podido conservar la ventaja que otorgaba el nuevo tanto de Llorente (ni más ni menos que el quinto en Anfield, donde empezó el idilio en 2020 para acabar tumbando al entonces campeón de Europa, la mitad de los diez que ha firmado en la máxima competición continental vestido de rojiblanco), en el Atlético, saben por su propia experiencia cómo levantarse de este traspié. De hecho, si sigue echando la mirada atrás, en el debut de la temporada 23-24 un gol de Barrios en Roma frente a la Lazio tampoco acabó con triunfo (1-1), lo que no impidió que los de Simeone acabaran alcanzando unos cuartos en los que el Dortmund sería su verdugo pese al triunfo de la ida en el Metropolitano. El que tampoco encontraba consuelo, por más que sus cifras en Anfield empiecen a ser paranormales, fue Llorente. “No puede ser que marque aquí otra vez. Muy feliz de marca aquí, pero cuando el equipo no gana y eres mayor te da exactamente igual”, señalaba. “La primera parte ha sido muy buena. Corriendo al espacio y asociándonos bien. Te vas con nada y te da igual todo lo demás”, añadí a anteponiendo el sinsabor del equipo a su brillo individual. Una actuación que volvería a llevarle a ejercer de comodín en busca de aprovechar su estado de dulce. “El míster confía que hay varias posiciones que podemos desempeñar. Me adapto a lo que pide el míster que es el que manda”, apuntaba antes de lamentar que todo se fuera al traste en la segunda mitad. “Hemos empezado muy bien, hemos hecho un gol aquí que es muy difícil. Ellos nos han apretado, nos han metido atrás y han empatado. La segunda parte ha sido de ellos. nos ha faltado energía para hacerle daño con los robos”, zanjó.

articles.title: Araujo: "El Barça está volando, es uno de los favoritos para ganar la Champions"
articles.standfirst: El central, cedido al Liverpool, también debutó con victoria en la máxima competición europea
articles.summary: El central, cedido al Liverpool, también debutó con victoria en la máxima competición europea
articles.body: Ronald Araujo elogió al Barcelona tras el encuentro de anoche contra el Atlético de Madrid. El central, cedido al Liverpool este verano, fue titular, completó los 90 minutos y se estrenó con victoria. Además, dio una bonita asistencia a Dominik Szoboszlai que se convirtió en el empate. "El Barcelona es uno de los favoritos para ganar la Liga de Campeones. Está volando", aseguró el uruguayo. Los catalanes, precisamente, jugaron antes que el Atlético de Madrid y ganaron 5-1 al Feyenoord en el Spotify Camp Nou. "Lo estoy siguiendo. Estoy muy feliz por mis compañeros de equipo. Tienen un gran equipo. Siempre los acompaño y estoy realmente encantado con lo que están viviendo en este momento", añadió. Araujo también está teniendo protagonismo en el conjunto inglés. De hecho, ha sido titular y ha completado los 90 minutos en los dos últimos encuentros del Liverpool, contra el Ipswich Town y ayer miércoles contra el Atlético de Madrid. En ambos partidos, se llevó el triunfo. El pasado 10 de agosto, el central llegó al conjunto de la Premier League. El bloque inglés asume la ficha del zaguero, de 27 años, y se aseguró una opción de compra de 55 millones de euros.

articles.title: "El Barcelona es el equipo más en forma de Europa"
articles.standfirst: Yon Cuezva analiza en La Tribu el gran arranque del equipo azulgrana, tras golear al Feyenoord en Champions
articles.summary: Yon Cuezva analiza en La Tribu el gran arranque del equipo azulgrana, tras golear al Feyenoord en Champions
articles.body: Yon Cuezva, Antonio Sanz, Amalio Moratalla, Paul Tenorio, Javi Lázaro y Ferran Martínez han sido los tertulianos de este jueves en La Tribu, patrocinada por Sportium durante esta temporada, para analizar el gran arranque de temporada del Barcelona, que goleó al Feyenoord, y la derrota del Atlético de Madrid ante el Liverpool, con Julián Álvarez como titular. Yon Cuezva fue uno de los más contundentes a la hora de analizar el momento azulgrana y compararlo con el del Real Madrid: "Ahora mismo, hay un abismo entre el Barça, que es un equipo, y el Madrid, que es una colección de grandes futbolistas. Veremos si el Barça es capaz de mantenerlo". Cuezva destacó tanto la planificación de la plantilla como el rendimiento que está consiguiendo el entrenador culé: "El debate es si este es el mejor Barça de Flick que hemos visto. Tiene gol, talento, hambre, presiona como muy pocos equipos en Europa. ¿Cuánto va a ser capaz de mantener esto Flick?". Una superioridad que resumió con una frase: "Ahora mismo el Barça es el equipo más en forma de Europa". Antonio Sanz también se mostró sorprendido por el nivel alcanzado por el conjunto azulgrana: "Su rendimiento está siendo excelso. Es sorprendente cómo ha arrancado el Barça, está en un estado de ánimo estelar. Flick ha metido una turbina a los futbolistas. Este Barça vuela". Amalio Moratalla situó precisamente al entrenador como la figura fundamental de este inicio de temporada: "Flick es el verdadero líder de lo que está pasando. Da la sensación de que el Barça se va a dar un paseo". Además, añadió: "Ahora mismo da la sensación de ser un equipo intocable". Paul Tenorio también concedió una nota máxima al inicio azulgrana, aunque introdujo una advertencia sobre las dificultades que todavía tiene que afrontar: "Es innegable que el Barça está volando. Cuando se ponga cuesta arriba, veremos cómo responde la defensa. En este inicio de temporada han sacado un diez, pero ha sido muy fácil". Javi Lázaro puso el foco en el salto competitivo que ha dado la plantilla: "El mercado del Barça es muy bueno porque ha encontrado la capacidad de pelear por la Champions. La figura de Rodri es clave, recursos como Gordon, Adeyemi...". Para Lázaro, el equipo ya está entre los principales aspirantes europeos: "El gran salto del Barça es que es candidato, al menos está entre el top 3, a ganar la Liga de Campeones. Se le puede comparar con PSG, Bayern y compañía. Está dos cuerpos por delante de Madrid y Atlético". Raúl Fuentes coincidió en la mejora del equipo respecto al curso anterior: "La plantilla ha subido de nivel respecto al año pasado. Flick está convenciendo a sus futbolistas y estos creen en la idea de su entrenador. Cuesta sacarle puntos débiles al Barça". Ferran Martínez también destacó la profundidad de la plantilla: "Este Barça tiene un fondo de armario de primer nivel. Antes había más diferencia entre la unidad A y la unidad B. Esta sensación de fondo de armario, de rotaciones, de Barça reconocible juegue quien juegue no la tenía desde el Barça de Luis Enrique o el Barça de Guardiola". El periodista también puso el foco en el rendimiento de Raphinha: "Al ritmo que veo a este Raphinha, no sé si será necesario que el Barça vuelva a por Julián. El Barça tiene a un gran 9 con Raphinha, está rindiendo a nivel top".

articles.title: Pochettino reclama la Premier que el Tottenham perdió ante el Chelsea
articles.standfirst: Las sanciones por las irregularidades de la era Abramovich reabren el debate sobre el título de 2016-17: “Deberíamos haber sido campeones”
articles.summary: Las sanciones por las irregularidades de la era Abramovich reabren el debate sobre el título de 2016-17: “Deberíamos haber sido campeones”
articles.body: Casi una década después, la Premier League 2016-17 vuelve a estar en el centro de la polémica. Chelsea conquistó aquel campeonato con 93 puntos, siete más que el Tottenham dirigido por Mauricio Pochettino. Sin embargo, las sanciones posteriores por irregularidades cometidas durante la etapa de Roman Abramovich han cambiado la perspectiva sobre aquella temporada. Pochettino lo tiene claro: "si el Chelsea incumplió las reglas, el Tottenham debería ser reconocido como campeón", explicó el argentino al rotativo británico The Guardian. Una afirmación que, aunque no es nueva, golpea directamente a la historia reciente del fútbol inglés y que plantea una pregunta incómoda: ¿puede un título seguir perteneciendo a un club que posteriormente ha sido sancionado por infringir las normas? Las irregularidades, además, no son una simple sospecha. Chelsea reconoció ante la Football Association 74 infracciones relacionadas con agentes, intermediarios y operaciones vinculadas a jugadores. La investigación puso el foco en pagos y transacciones que no fueron comunicados correctamente a las autoridades durante la era Abramovich. La FA terminó sancionando al club con una multa de 10 millones de libras, mientras que la Premier League realizó su propia investigación y también confirmó incumplimientos. El caso ha sacado a la luz operaciones vinculadas a futbolistas como Eden Hazard, Willian, David Luiz y Nemanja Matic. Nombres que no son precisamente secundarios cuando hablamos del Chelsea de aquella época. Y aquí comienza la gran discusión. Chelsea fue sancionado, pero no perdió la Premier League 2016-17. Las autoridades no han establecido que aquellas infracciones justifiquen retirar los 93 puntos conseguidos por el equipo de Antonio Conte, ni que los pagos investigados hubieran permitido al club superar los límites financieros que habrían provocado una deducción de puntos. Con este escenario, Mauricio Pochettino plantea una cuestión difícil de ignorar. ¿De qué sirve castigar una infracción si el resultado deportivo obtenido durante el periodo afectado permanece completamente intacto? El argumento del argentino es esencialmente deportivo y moral: si un club incumple las reglas mientras sus rivales las respetan, la competición deja de desarrollarse en condiciones completamente iguales. El Tottenham terminó segundo y fue el gran rival del Chelsea durante aquella campaña. De ahí que Pochettino (que no olvidemos no hace el Chelsea fue su último club antes de coger las riendas de la selección de Estados Unidos) considere que los Spurs deberían beneficiarse de cualquier eventual sanción que desposeyera al Chelsea del campeonato. El problema es que el reglamento no establece que el segundo clasificado se convierta automáticamente en campeón cada vez que el ganador es sancionado años después.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo vs Travis Kelce: The stunning $1.11 billion net worth gap between the football icon and Kansas City Chiefs superstar
articles.summary: Off the field News: Cristiano Ronaldo and Travis Kelce have both built commercial empires well beyond their playing careers, yet the money involved tells two very differe.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo and Travis Kelce have both built commercial empires well beyond their playing careers, yet the money involved tells two very different stories.Celebrity Net Worth puts Ronaldo's fortune at $1.2 billion. Kelce, by comparison, is valued at $90 million. Do the maths and Ronaldo is worth more than thirteen times as much as the Chiefs tight end, a gap of roughly $1.11 billion.Ronaldo's billion-dollar riseRonaldo crossed into billionaire territory in June 2025 after agreeing a contract extension with Al Nassr, one that is among the most lucrative in sporting history. His salary there is put at $224 million a year, and once endorsements are folded in, his total annual income for the 2026 World Cup year is estimated at around $300 million.Salary alone barely scratches the surface, though. The CR7 brand now stretches across hotels, fitness and fashion, among other ventures, built up over years of parallel investment alongside his football earnings. His relationship with Nike matters here too: Celebrity Net Worth cites a reported $1 billion lifetime deal as one of the anchors of his overall wealth.Add it all up and, by the time he eventually hangs up his boots, his career earnings from salary and endorsements combined are projected to comfortably clear $2 billion.Kelce's $90 million storyKelce's path looks nothing like it. He has spent his whole NFL career at Kansas City since being taken in the third round of the 2013 draft, and has since become one of the finest tight ends the league has produced, part of a Chiefs core that won Super Bowls LIV, LVII and LVIII.By the end of the 2025 season his NFL earnings sat at roughly $111.2 million in salary and bonuses. His 2026 deal should push that career total to around $123.2 million if he sees the season through. For this year alone, he's guaranteed $12 million in cash from Kansas City, with incentives capable of lifting his total compensation to somewhere near $15 million.Football is no longer the whole picture for him, either. Television work, endorsements, investments, and above all his podcast "New Heights", co-hosted with brother Jason, have all added to the ledger. Then there's the Taylor Swift factor: since the pair started dating in 2023, Kelce's profile has exploded well past the usual NFL crowd, and with it, the commercial opportunities have followed.Side by sideRonaldo: $1.2 billionKelce: $90 millionGap: roughly $1.11 billionKelce has pulled in more than $111 million from football wages and bonuses alone, which by any normal standard is a serious fortune. Set against Ronaldo's number, though, it's a fraction.Most of that gap comes down to time and scale. Ronaldo has spent two decades constructing arguably the most recognisable personal brand in world sport, layering elite wages on top of endorsement deals and a genuinely global business portfolio. Kelce, by contrast, has only really become a crossover name in the last few years.Part of that is down to the sports themselves. Football's reach is planetary in a way the NFL, for all its domestic power, still isn't, and that difference shows up directly in the size of Ronaldo's commercial footprint compared with Kelce's. His wealth doesn't depend on match-day salary in the way a lot of American athletes' does; it runs on social following, sponsorship and business interests that would tick along even if he stopped playing tomorrow.None of which makes Kelce's $90 million look anything other than serious money. It's just that next to Ronaldo's $1.2 billion, even a fortune like his ends up looking modest.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Por qué hay tres días de partidos en la primera jornada de Champions League
articles.standfirst: Algo que solo sucede en la jornada inaugural
articles.summary: Algo que solo sucede en la jornada inaugural
articles.body: La UEFA Champions League estrenó hace tres temporadas un formato revolucionario en su fase de liga que ha transformado de forma radical el calendario habitual del fútbol europeo. Una de las novedades más destacadas y que más ha llamado la atención de los aficionados en el arranque de la competición es la distribución de la primera jornada, la cual se extiende de forma excepcional a lo largo de tres días: martes, miércoles y jueves. Este cambio rompe con la tradición histórica del torneo, que siempre había concentrado sus encuentros europeos de clubes exclusivamente en las noches de martes y miércoles. La razón principal detrás de esta decisión responde a la implantación del concepto denominado por la UEFA como 'semana exclusiva'. En el nuevo modelo de competición, cada una de las tres grandes torneos continentales —la Champions League, la Europa League y la Conference League— cuenta con una semana en el calendario reservada íntegramente para su uso y disfrute. De esta manera, durante la primera fecha del torneo, la máxima competición europea no comparte protagonismo con ninguna otra prueba internacional, permitiendo expandir su cobertura televisiva y ofrecer una mayor cantidad de franjas horarias a los espectadores de todo el mundo. Esta estrategia no solo obedece a razones de visibilidad deportiva, sino que responde a un potente pilar económico y de entretenimiento. Al distribuir los 18 partidos inaugurales a lo largo de tres jornadas consecutivas, los operadores con derechos de televisión consiguen evitar la masiva saturación de encuentros simultáneos. Esto permite a los aficionados disfrutar de un mayor número de partidos en directo sin tener que elegir entre ellos, lo que se traduce directamente en un incremento notable de las audiencias globales y en un mayor retorno publicitario para los clubes y la propia organización. Cabe señalar que esta dispersión en tres días es un privilegio reservado de manera única para la jornada inaugural de la Champions League. A partir de la segunda fecha y hasta la penúltima de la fase de liga, el torneo volverá a su formato habitual de dos días (martes y miércoles), devolviendo los jueves a la Europa League y la Conference League.

articles.title: La final de la EH Txapela anticipa el primer derbi del curso al 2 de octubre en Anoeta
articles.standfirst: Real y Athletic se verán las caras en un partido con muchas bajas por el parón internacional, sobre todo en el equipo txuriurdin, y que servirá de homenaje a Mikel Etxarri
articles.summary: Real y Athletic se verán las caras en un partido con muchas bajas por el parón internacional, sobre todo en el equipo txuriurdin, y que servirá de homenaje a Mikel Etxarri
articles.body: Real Sociedad y Athletic se verán las caras antes de la undécima jornada de LaLiga que marcaba el primer derbi de la temporada para el fin de semana del 31 de octubre y el 1 de noviembre, ya que la final de la Euskal Herria Txapela, el torneo que cuenta sólo los resultados de los equipos vascos, ha sido designada para el viernes 2 de octubre a las 19.00 horas en Anoeta. El encuentro servirá de homenaje a Mikel Etxarri, ex director deportivo del club txuriurdin y seleccionador de la Euskal Selekzioa. Será un duelo descafeinado, eso sí, ya que faltarán los internacionales, que por parte de la Real apuntan a ser alrededor de una decena, si son llamados por sus respectivos países Aramburu, Jon Martín, Óskarsson, Oyarzabal, Guedes, Ochieng, Kubo, Herrera y Sucic, entre otros. En el lado del Athletic faltarán los campeones del mundo (Simón, Nico y Laporte) mientras que quedará por ver cuál es el planteamiento de Ghana con Iñaki Williams, que estuvo en el pasado Mundial, y de México respecto a Padilla. La tricolor ha cambiado de técnico y Padilla formó en la lista de preparación mundialista, aunque no estuvo convocado. El encuentro, además de para que los menos habituales hasta entonces en la Real y el Athletic tengan minutos de competición, servirá para homenajear a Mikel Etxarri, en su día director deportivo de la entidad guipuzcoana y seleccionador de Euskadi, y ante todo una persona muy apreciada en ambos clubes por sus conocimientos de fútbol.

articles.title: Barcelona defender putting in extra work to return to his best and win back Flick’s trust
articles.summary: One of the most notable changes at FC Barcelona this season has been Jules Kounde’s loss of prominence in the team.The Frenchman has lost his starting status...
articles.body:
One of the most notable changes at FC Barcelona this season has been Jules Kounde 's loss of prominence in the team.

The Frenchman has lost his starting status in the lineup under Hansi Flick , with Eric Garcia becoming the first-choice at right-back.

In fact, during the summer, the Blaugrana sporting department was prepared to consider his departure if an attractive offer arrived as the defender was no longer considered untouchable.

So far in the 2026/27 season, the 27-year-old star has only started two games out of five for Barça, with one of them coming because Garcia was unavailable due to suspension.

Now, according to SPORT , Kounde is fully aware that he is not currently at his best and that he must earn Flick's confidence again.

As such, the French international has been putting in extra work in training to regain his lost prominence.

Kounde has lost his place in the team. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

Kounde has always been obsessive about maintaining peak physical condition and has regularly added individual work to Barcelona 's scheduled sessions.

The report states that he has been staying behind after first-team training sessions finish.

While his teammates head into the dressing room, the Frenchman continues working on the pitch alongside the club's fitness coaches and physiotherapists.

The objective is straightforward: recover his best form and re-establish himself in a position where he has lost prominence.

Kounde knows exactly where he stands, and his response has been to work even harder.

As well as pushing himself in the gym, he is extending his working days at the Ciutat Esportiva in an attempt to rediscover the form that once made him one of the world's leading full-backs.

This increased workload is not simply a reaction to his recent decline in form.

Not giving up easily. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

Kounde was following a similar routine when he was arguably enjoying the best period of his career, with several major European clubs, including Manchester City , monitoring his situation.

The Frenchman has long worked with personal fitness coaches outside Barcelona's official sessions.

He was previously spotted on several occasions training at the athletics track in Sitges at around 6:30 or 7:00 in the morning, several hours before arriving at the Ciutat Esportiva to train with his teammates.

That routine says plenty about Kounde's mentality. He worked relentlessly when he was an undisputed starter, and he continues to do so now that his position has become less secure.

Kounde knows he has lost ground and that regaining his place in the starting XI will not be easy. But he has already begun fighting for it.

articles.body:
The match officials for Monday's Premier League clash with Newcastle have been announced, with Michael Salisbury set to take charge at Elland Road.

The Lancashire-based official is vastly experienced in English football, working his way up from National League North level all the way to the top-flight, where he has featured 59 times to date.

The Whites have a mixed record from the six games overseen by Salisbury, winning two of those and drawing once. Two of those encounters came last campaign, and one came in the EFL Championship as the Whites dismantled Cardiff City 7-0.

Most recently, the 41-year-old officiated the dramatic 2-2 draw away at Bournemouth last campaign, Sean Longstaff on target to secure a late equaliser on the South Coast.

Newcastle have also seen Salisbury take to the pitch on six occasions, overseeing three wins and two draws.

Running the touchlines are Adam Nunn & Nick Hopton with Tom Nield appointed as Fourth Official. Keeping up with the action from Stockley Park is VAR John Brooks and Additional VAR James Mainwaring.

Assistant referees: Adam Nunn & Nick Hopton

articles.title: Nebraska running back Jamal Rule named Week 1 Standout
articles.summary: Nebraska football running back Jamal Rule was named a weekly standout for his performance on Saturday.
articles.body:
Nebraska football running back Jamaal Rule was named one of Charles Power's Week 1 True Freshman Standouts . Rule headlines the list, alongside USC wide receiver Trent Mosley , Ohio State corner Jay Timmons, Tennessee quarterback Fazion Brandon, and Washington defensive lineman Derek Colman-Brusa.

This is the second accolade this week for Rule, who was also named the Big Ten freshman of the week on Monday. The running back had a tremendous game against Ohio on Saturday, carrying the ball 15 times for 122 yards.

Rule also caught two passes for 47 yards and a touchdown. In total, he accumulated 169 yards and three touchdowns from the line of scrimmage, in what was a big day.

Rule was certainly able to set the tone for the Huskers both on the field and in the running back room. It will be fun to see what he does in a follow-up act this week against Bowling Green.

articles.title: Angel Reese-Caitlin Clark connection tops USA vs Hungary winners and losers
articles.summary: The college rivals-turned-teammates were a two-woman show. Clark and Reese helped the USA breeze into the FIBA Women's World Cup semifinals.
articles.body:
Team USA punched its ticket to the FIBA Women's World Cup semifinal round in convincing fashion.

The Americans dismantled Hungary in a 108-56 quarterfinal blowout win in Berlin, Germany, on Thursday, Sept. 10, where they led for all but 19 seconds to extend their World Cup win streak to 34 straight games. It was USA's largest margin of victory in the tournament thus far, with every USA player scoring for the third time.

"This is one of our most compete performances," USA head coach Kara Lawson said.

The Americans move on to face the winner of Spain-Australia in the semifinals on Saturday, Aug. 12.

The red, white and blue victory was so complete it was hard to narrow down a list of winners. Hungary headlines Thursday's losers after coming up short in the semifinals.

USA TODAY Sports rounded up the highlights and lowlights from Thursday's quarterfinal match between USA and Hungary:

Team USA looking for gold at FIBA Women's World Cup

After the American's scare against Italy in the preliminary round, Napheesa Collier and Breanna Stewart said it was their responsibility as veterans to get Team USA, made up of seven newcomers, off to a good start.

"Obviously we're two of the older people on the team… we have to be able to set the tone and set an example," Collier said on Monday. That's exactly what she did Thursday's quarterfinal game against Hungary.

Collier came out aggressive with 10 points, three rebounds and one block in the first quarter. She rejected Minnesota Lynx teammate Dorka Juhasz's shot. By the third quarter, Collier improved her stat line to 19 points and seven rebounds while shooting 9-of-13 from the field and 1-of-2 from the 3-point line. And after 15 minutes of play, her job was done.

It was Collier's highest-scoring game in a Team USA jersey, including the 2020 and 2024 Olympics, where Collier helped the Americans win gold.

Collier started playing again in July after undergoing offseason surgery on both ankles.

The Caitlin Clark -Angel Reese connection

The college rivals-turned-teammates were a two-woman show on Thursday. Clark found Reese under the basket early and often and Reese found the bottom of the net in Thursday's win. Clark assisted on six of Reese's nine points and Reese returned the favor. Reese secured a steal and set Clark up for a transition layup in the third quarter.

"We've played against each other so many times. I'm sure we know each other's game like the back of each other's hand," Reese said after the win. "Just easily dishing it off to her. She dishes off to me. She knows my spots. I kinda got one to her today, maybe two. So it's fun. We just continue to build chemistry because we know we're gonna be USA teammates for a while."

Clark finished with 10 points and nine assists, just one assist shy of her second double-double of the tournament. Reese had nine points, six rebounds, three assists and two steals.

Team USA's chemistry is building, as evidenced by the team's record-breaking performance. The Americans collectively tallied 31 assists on 40-made field goals in their win over Hungary, which set a record for the most assists in a World Cup quarterfinal match.

"Having (31) assists really speaks to the game, the way that we're moving the ball," Collier said. "It's not one-on-one basketball. We're playing as a team. Multiple people are getting touches. We're finding the best shot, not just a good shot. And so that reflects that.

"Each game, again, we're improving with that, just getting our chemistry. This team has never played together with this group of people. And so sometimes it takes a while to come together, but we're taking advantage of each practice, each game that we have and getting better."

Remember when USA went 1-of-12 from the 3-point line in its 55-52 win over Italy on Monday? Well, the Americans exercised those demons and shot a staggering 12-of-23 from beyond the arc on Thursday.

Aliyah Boston showed her range early, knocking down back-to-back 3s in the first quarter to help build USA's lead. Rhyne Howard , who leads the WNBA in made 3-pointers this season, had the hot hand in the second half. She finished shooting 3-of-5 from deep. Howard was one of four players to make at least two 3-pointers.

2026 WNBA season is underway. See photos from the league's 30th year

The unceremonious end to Hungary's dream run

It's a little sad to imagine the hopeful Hungary fans who tuned into Thursday's matchup with the excitement of what had been a fantastic run.

This was Hungary's first World Cup appearance since 1998, and their first time in the tournament's final eight since 1986.

When 19th ranked Hungary never trailed in its win over world No. 10 Japan 84–63 on Tuesday, there was reason to believe the unlikely run could continue — especially since Team USA showed cracks in its narrow win over Italy.

That optimism was quickly crushed, as unbeaten Team USA was so dominant the game got out of hand quickly. The U.S. led by as many as 32 points in the first half as they scored at will and held Hungary to 32% shooting from the field.

Team USA coach Kara Lawson received her share of criticism for sticking with her starting lineup of veterans throughout the group stage. Against Hungary, those detractors were left with nothing to lament.

When asked entering Thursday's matchup if she'd consider starting World Cup debutant Caitlin Clark, Lawson was firm in saying she believed her opening group had "done a really good job."

When pushed with a follow-up about whether she'd put fellow newcomers Angel Reese and Paige Bueckers in the opening rotation, Lawson started firm and repeated part of her previous answer: "I like where we are right now."

Starters Chelsea Gray , Jackie Young , Kahleah Copper , Napheesa Collier and Breanna Stewart didn't disappoint, getting the U.S. off to a 36-12 lead by the end of the first quarter on 74% shooting from the field and 3-of-3 shooting from deep.

Fans of the Young and Turnt crew were still fed from start to finish. Clark connected with Reese ahead of the buzzer in the first frame, and that chemistry continued throughout as every single Team USA player scored in the blowout, which resulted in the largest margin of victory in this World Cup for the U.S.

Hungary had trouble getting any offense going inside despite to post play of 6-foot-5 forward Dorka Juhasz and 6-4 center Virag Takacs-Kiss. The pair were held to two points each and Team USA outscored Hungary 52-16 in the paint.

"They're both excellent players, and they did maybe miss some jump shots that they normally make, especially Dorka, I thought, had some quality looks in that first half, and they just didn't go down," USA coach Kara Lawson said. "But I felt like we were really confident in our game plan, and Napheesa (Collier) and (Breanna Stewart) did a good job defensively. Aliyah (Boston) and Angel (Reese) when they came in, Kiki (Iriafen) as well.

"We were able to rotate, you know, we have five forwards that all bring something different to the table and bring an athleticism."

Every basketball fan who woke up to watch USA vs Hungary

If you woke up at 5:30 a.m. ET to watch the United States hoop against Hungary, congratulations, you're the real MVP. That level of dedication needs to be studied. Watching basketball before 8 a.m. local time feels like it should be illegal. We all need a nap.

Truthfully, this likely feels like complaining to the people who live overseas and do this regularly to watch their favorite teams. Please allow us three business days to get all our grievances out of our systems. We are not used to this kind of stress. Please respect our privacy as we cope.

Saturday, Sept. 12: USA vs. Spain/Australia (Semifinal) | TBS, truTV (TBD)

The Women's World Cup final and third-place game will be held on Sunday, Sept. 13 (TNT, truTV).

articles.title: Mind coach and VR Glasses: Benjamin Sesko pulling out all the stops to win back starting spot
articles.summary: 1Benjamin Sesko is in line to make his first start of the season when Manchester United host Sabah in their Champions League opener tonight.The striker score...
articles.body:
Benjamin Sesko is in line to make his first start of the season when Manchester United host Sabah in their Champions League opener tonight.

The striker scored after replacing Matheus Cunha during Sunday's 2-2 draw at Everton , strengthening his case as Michael Carrick considers how to manage his squad before the Manchester derby.

United have taken four points from their opening three league matches against Hull City, Ipswich Town and Everton, with Carrick deploying a 4-2-3-1 formation.

Bryan Mbeumo operated through the middle during pre-season before moving to the right following Amad 's injury. Cunha has subsequently filled the false-nine role.

Sesko was given time off during the summer to recover from the shin problem which ended his first campaign at Old Trafford prematurely. He did not feature during pre-season and has been introduced as a substitute in each of United's first three competitive games.

Thursday's fixture is followed by the 199th Manchester derby at Old Trafford on Sunday, leaving Carrick with decisions to make over the workloads of his attacking players.

The Daily Mail reports that Sesko will hope to receive his opportunity against Sabah , particularly after Cunha offered little threat at Everton.

United were outshot 18-14 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium and recorded a lower expected-goals total than their hosts. Cunha missed a first-half opportunity before being replaced by the Slovenian.

Sesko gave United a more conventional focal point and headed home Luke Shaw 's cross, although Ainsley Maitland-Niles later equalised.

Carrick said : "Ben's obviously getting closer and closer. Since the Liverpool game at the end of April is a long time to miss. We've had to look after him to get him fit."

The head coach added: "He's probably trained three and a bit weeks fully with no restrictions. I think you can see that, coming onto the pitch and getting his rhythm."

Carrick stopped short of confirming a start but said Sesko would be involved in every game, adding that it was now a question of when the forward takes "that next step". Slovenian broadcaster 24ur Sport considers the Sabah fixture the "perfect opportunity".

Sesko joined United from RB Leipzig for £74 million. After scoring twice under Ruben Amorim, he struck three goals across Darren Fletcher's two matches as caretaker coach .

Another seven goals arrived in 13 games under Carrick, even though Sesko started the first six of those matches on the bench. A run of four consecutive starts followed before injury intervened.

The 6ft 5in forward has returned with a noticeably more muscular physique. His home contains a gym, swimming pool, ice bath and sauna, while his recovery work also includes a hyperbaric chamber and red-light therapy.

Sesko additionally uses virtual-reality glasses to simulate match situations and works with a mind coach, with meditation another part of his preparation. Amorim previously described him as a "control freak".

Following his goal at Everton, Sesko said: "It's nice to be back. It's the best feeling when I'm scoring, especially like that. It's my job to provide goals and points for the team."

Carrick must now decide whether Sesko's fitness and impact from the bench justify changing an attacking structure used throughout the summer. Sabah appears to offer the clearest opening yet for the striker to return to the starting XI.

Sesko is pushing for his first start of the season against Sabah.

He scored as a substitute during the 2-2 draw at Everton.

Carrick says the striker has trained without restrictions for over three weeks.

The Slovenian scored seven goals in 13 games under Carrick last season.

articles.title: UConn great Napheesa Collier leads Team USA over Hungary to advance to World Cup semifinals
articles.summary: The former UConn star scored 19 points as Team USA set an assist record for the World Cup quarterfinals.
articles.body:
It didn't matter that it's her World Cup debut or that her WNBA teammate wore the opposing team's uniform; Napheesa Collier was unstoppable.

The former UConn women's basketball star dominated on both ends of the floor to lead Team USA to its 12 th consecutive World Cup semifinal appearance.

Thanks to Collier's game-high 19 points, the United States shut down fellow former Husky star and Collier's Minnesota Lynx teammate Dorka Juhász to defeat Hungary, 108-56 , in Thursday's World Cup quarterfinals in Berlin, Germany.

The Americans will face the winner of Spain-Australia (2:30 p.m. on Thursday) in Saturday's semifinal (time TBD) for a chance to move on to Sunday's gold-medal game.

Led by Collier, five players finished in double-digit scoring for Team USA. Caitlin Clark dished out a game-high nine assists, while Collier, Kahleah Copper and Angel Reese each finished with six rebounds.

Fellow Huskies Breanna Stewart (eight points, three rebounds, two assists) and Paige Bueckers (seven points, three assists, one rebound and one steal) were two of 10 players with five points or more for the U.S.

Hungary, which last reached the World Cup quarterfinals in 1986 (also lost to the U.S.), was led by Reka Lelik with 12 points and Juhász with a game-high eight rebounds. Juhász, who was named the EuroLeague MVP in April, averaged double-doubles in Hungary's first four games of this year's tournament, but finished Thursday's game with just two points on 1-of-12 shooting for her worst performance of the tournament.

The United States punched first and punched hard to open Thursday's quarterfinals. Collier set the tone on both ends. First, the Minnesota Lynx superstar blocked her WNBA teammate, Juhász, two minutes into the game. Then, Collier went off on offense and scored a game-high 10 points in the first 10 minutes.

Hungary couldn't keep up and failed to defend Collier's signature step-back fadeaway as the former Husky put the U.S. up by 20 with a little over a minute left in the frame thanks to her go-to shot. Stewart also got in on the fun, even scoring the first bucket of the day. The former UConn teammates combined for nine of Team USA's first 13 points, 15 of its first 36 and 17 of its first 59.

The U.S. used an 18-3 run to break open the game in the first quarter and successfully shut down Juhász early. The Hungary star, who led all players with five rebounds at halftime, missed her first seven shots and didn't score her first basket until the 2:26 mark in the second quarter.

Team USA pressured Juhász and Hungary's entire frontcourt hard in the paint. Thanks to its aggressive defense and Collier and Stewart, the U.S. had more points in the paint (32) than Hungary (30) had total points at halftime (Team USA led 32-4 in the paint at intermission).

The Americans led by as much as 34 in the first half, scoring 25 points off Hungary's 14 first-half turnovers and shooting 65% from the floor.

Collier, who finished 9-of-13 from the floor with six rebounds, chipped in nine more points in the first six minutes of the third quarter to push the U.S.'s lead to over 40. Her 19 total points marked her best-ever when playing for Team USA's senior national team in a non-qualifying event.

Thursday's win extends Team USA's World Cup win streak to 34 straight games across the last two decades. The Americans finished Thursday with a 59 field goal percentage, 42 rebounds, 17 steals and 44 points off Hungary's 27 turnovers. Team USA outscored Hungary 52-16 in the paint. The U.S.'s 31 assists set the record for the most in a World Cup quarterfinal game.

After finishing group phase 3-0, the U.S. saved its best for the knockout round. Its 108 points and 52-point win against Hungary marked Team USA's highest-scoring game and largest margin of victory so far in this year's World Cup.

articles.title: Drew Lock admits he’d never practiced key touchdown play
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks had to turn to backup quarterback Drew Lock during Wednesday night’s season opener against the New England Patriots after starter Sam Da...
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks had to turn to backup quarterback Drew Lock during Wednesday night's season opener against the New England Patriots after starter Sam Darnold went down with an injury. He delivered, leading the team to a 13-10 victory, even if he didn't know all of the plays.

During his postgame press conference, Lock openly admitted that he had actually never practiced one of the key plays that gave the team the victory.

During the third quarter of Wednesday's win over the New England Patriots, the Seahawks faced a crucial fourth-and-1 from the Patriots' 45-yard line with just under 12 minutes to play in the game.

The Seahawks dialed up a play-action pass to wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba that not only got them the first down, but Smith-Njigba was able to find room to run, taking it all the way to the end zone.

The play tied the game at 10, and the Seahawks would go on to take the lead for good with a field goal on the next possession.

What's interesting, however, is that Lock admitted after the game that he actually never had a chance to run that play during practice.

"It is like a classic football play," Lock said, via the team's website . "But, no. No, definitely never ran it. Looked kind of funny before the snap. I didn't really seem like they had anybody ready to match Jaxon based on what I knew we were about it run. He's the third read in that play, and when 11 is just standing there, you got to give him the pill."

Lock got off to a slow start in the game, but he praised the team's defense for keeping the game close enough for him to simply get the ball to his playmakers in space, just as he did on that play.

"Knowing the type of defense that we have, there is no rush to push the ball down the field," Lock said. "Let's find ways to get the ball in our guys' hands. Now, when the ones down field are there, I've never been one to be afraid of those, but having the mindset of taking football, getting it in our guys' hands. You got the best defense in the world, in my opinion, let's keep the ball moving forward and see what the scoreboard looks like at the end of this."

Ultimately, it worked, and Lock was able to lead his team to victory.

articles.title: Manchester United scouted Mbappe but didn’t sign him, says Ryan Giggs
articles.summary: Former United assistant coach reveals his pursuit of a teenage Mbappe after a tip-off from a French scout.
articles.body:
One of the world’s most prolific goal scorers, Kylian Mbappe, could have signed a contract with Manchester United when he was a little-known teenager in the French league, but the English Premier League club’s scouts decided against approaching his then-club, Monaco, former United player and coach Ryan Giggs has revealed.

Giggs, who was United’s interim and assistant coach between 2014 and 2016, made the revelation on a podcast with his former United teammate Rio Ferdinand on Wednesday.

Mbappe has several club and international goal-scoring records to his name and now plays for European football giants Real Madrid in Spain.

The 27-year-old signed for the La Liga team in 2024 from French league champions Paris Saint-Germain, who scooped him up from Monaco in 2018 after Mbappe lit up Ligue 1 with his speed and goal-scoring accuracy.

But according to Giggs, Mbappe could have been a Red Devil had the club’s scouts pursued him after watching him play in 2015.

The United legend said he was in southern France in 2015 when he was approached by a local football scout and tipped off about a rising star.

“I was walking along the beach back to the hotel and all of a sudden I can feel someone coming up to me,” Giggs said while narrating his meeting with the scout.

“He comes up to me and says, ‘I just wanted to just say hello. I’m a big United fan and big fan of yours. I watch a lot of youth football in France and you have to look at this player. He’s called Kylian Mbappe. He’s at Monaco and I think he’s a player for Man United.'”

According to Giggs, who was manager Louis van Gaal’s assistant coach at the time, the scout then asked for his email address and wrote to him a few weeks later with details about Mbappe.

It prompted Giggs and fellow United assistant coach Albert Stuivenberg to watch Mbappe play in Monaco’s youth team, only to be taken aback by Mbappe’s brilliance.

“We were just like, ‘Wow! What is this?’,” the former winger recalled.

“You see players and they can be special, and he [Mbappe] did look exceptional.”

The two assistant managers then asked United’s scouting team to watch him, but they never ended up pursuing the player who went on to become a world champion and two-time FIFA Golden Boot award winner with France.

“Someone in France [from the scouting team] went to watch him when Monaco were playing PSG in Paris,” Giggs carried on. “A few weeks later I said to this guy, ‘How did it go?’ He went, ‘Yeah, they weren’t too sure about him.’ So I just went, ‘All right, OK.’ And that was it.”

Mbappe’s career took off a year after United’s failure to pursue him, as the then-16-year-old scored 26 goals in 44 appearances for Monaco in their French title-winning 2016-17 season, including six in their run to the UEFA Champions League semifinals.

The teen sensation was loaned to PSG in the following season before securing a permanent move in the 2018-19 season. He went on to score 256 goals in 308 appearances for the French champions, winning the Ligue 1 title six times.

The France national team captain won the World Cup in 2018 in Russia and finished runners-up to Argentina four years later in Qatar, where he scored a hat-trick in the final and won his first Golden Boot Award.

articles.title: French Football Federation withdraws support for FIFA President Infantino
articles.summary: FFF aligns position with of other European federations, such as Belgium, England, Italy, Scotland, and Sweden.
articles.body:
The French Football Federation is withdrawing its support for Gianni Infantino’s re-election bid as FIFA chief ⁠next year, FFF President Philippe Diallo has said, saying trust in the head of world football’s governing body had been broken.

The decision was taken unanimously by the FFF’s executive committee, Diallo ⁠said on Thursday.

“The trust placed in the FIFA president has been broken,” Diallo told reporters. “The way in which we envisage the running of world football no longer corresponds with the way it is being conducted.”

Infantino, who is seeking another term as FIFA president, has faced mounting criticism since his failed proposal to sell a ‌20 percent stake in FIFA competitions, including the World Cup, to private investors was abandoned in July following widespread opposition from football’s regional confederations.

Diallo said France had initially backed Infantino’s candidacy at the end of June, when he was the only declared candidate, but that subsequent events had fundamentally changed the circumstances.

“The conditions for our support for his candidacy were no longer there,” he said.

Diallo added that the proposed stake sale, which emerged without what he described as proper ⁠consultation or information being provided to federations, had raised serious questions over ⁠FIFA’s governance and decision-making.

Several European federations, including England’s and Italy’s, have withdrawn their backing for Infantino since the collapse of his proposal.

UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation and North America’s CONCACAF have called for change at the top of FIFA and ⁠are seeking a credible alternative before the March election.

Diallo said France’s decision formed part of a broader movement within UEFA and beyond and that ⁠discussions would now focus on governance reform and finding a ⁠candidate capable of defeating Infantino.

“It is not enough simply to criticise if you want things to move forward. You also have to make proposals,” Diallo said.

He added that UEFA would need to define a platform for the next FIFA leadership cycle ‌and, when the time came, choose a candidate for the election.

“We will need to be ready by then to put forward a candidacy capable of winning the FIFA presidency,” Diallo said.

Infantino still has ‌the ‌support of South America’s CONMEBOL and Africa’s CAF.

The FIFA presidential election will take place in Rabat on March 18, 2027, with the deadline for candidacies on November 18.

articles.title: Should Chelsea be stripped of 2016-17 title and Tottenham crowned champions?
articles.summary: Does Mauricio Pochettino have a case that Tottenham should be retrospectively crowned Premier League champions?
articles.body:
Should Tottenham be retrospectively crowned Premier League champions for the 2016-17 season?

That's the opinion of former manager Mauricio Pochettino, who led Spurs to a second-place finish - seven points behind Chelsea - that season.

This is about Chelsea making £47m in secret payments, according to a Premier League investigation, to unregistered agents and third parties to seal transfers between 2011 and 2018.

The transfers included Eden Hazard, Samuel Eto'o, Willian, Ramires, David Luiz, Andre Schurrle and Nemanja Matic.

Four of those - Hazard, Willian, Luiz and Matic - were at the club in 2016-17.

During that period Chelsea won two Premier League titles (2014-15 and 2016-17), two FA Cups (2011-12 and 2017-18), the EFL Cup (2014-15) and the Europa League (2018–19).

Chelsea have been fined by Uefa, the Premier League and the Football Association, but Pochettino thinks that is not enough.

"If they admitted they broke the rules, the Premier League title was for the second-best team," Pochettino said.

Pochettino is one of the first people of significance to articulate what many feel - that Chelsea got off lightly with a fine.

Fans of Everton and Nottingham Forest have pointed out that their clubs faced points deductions for relatively small profit and sustainability breaches, while Chelsea sought to sign star players with secret payments.

Meanwhile, there is no sign of a verdict in the case of Manchester City's 115 charges for alleged breaches of Premier League financial rules.

Does Pochettino have a point? And how much of an impact did those four players have on the title race?

Hazard is seen as the poster boy for Chelsea 's breaches.

The Blues fought off most of Europe's top clubs to sign him from Lille for £32m in the summer of 2012.

Between May 2013 and August 2016, according to the investigation, seven payments totalling £5.6m were made to an unregistered agent "for the benefit of the club in connection with Hazard's transfer".

Pochettino's argument is that Spurs could have beaten other clubs to the signing of players of similar ability had they also ignored the rules.

What about Hazard's impact in the 2016-17 season?

The Belgium forward started 36 Premier League games, scored 16 goals and provided five assists. Only Cesar Azpilicueta started more matches, and only Diego Costa netted more goals (20).

Hazard was Chelsea 's player of the year, was named in the Professional Footballers' Association (PFA) team of the year, and made the shortlist for PFA player of the year.

Then there's the direct impact of his goals and assists in the results of four fixtures.

Hazard scored the first goal in a 2-1 win over West Ham in August, then scored a goal and provided an assist in a 2-0 victory over Southampton in November.

In March he scored the opener as Chelsea again beat the Hammers 2-1, and got both goals in a 2-0 win over Manchester City in April.

You could argue that input was worth 10 points.

There is no doubt that Hazard had a huge influence, but this was his fifth season at the club. It was not as if Chelsea signed him in the summer of 2016.

Willian - hugely influential bit-part role

Willian joined Chelsea from Anzhi Makhachkala in 2013, with the investigation finding that transfer fee payments totalling £19.2m were made to two unregistered entities in connection with his move and that of Samuel Eto'o.

Willian was not a regular starter in 2016-17, with 19 of his 34 appearances coming from the bench.

But he still had a huge influence, scoring eight goals and providing eight assists.

The Brazilian's attacking returns were crucial in four matches.

He had an assist in a 1-0 win at Sunderland in December. He scored two goals in a 4-2 victory over Stoke in December, and the first goal as Chelsea beat Stoke 2-1 in March. He provided an assist for the winning goal in a 4-3 victory over Watford in May.

His contributions helped Chelsea take eight points from those fixtures.

Crucially, Chelsea nipped in at the last minute to sign Willian from under the noses of Spurs, who might argue that was only because of the secret payments.

Matic and Luiz - players who left and came back

The investigation found that Chelsea made payments totalling £5.1m between 2012 and 2015 "to provide talent identification services in certain European countries".

This was identified as payments in relation to the registrations of Ramires, Luiz, Schurrle and Matic.

However, by 2016-17 Matic and Luiz were in their second spells at Chelsea . The deal with Benfica which meant Matic and Luiz swapped clubs in 2011 was looked into.

Matic returned to Stamford Bridge in 2014, with Luiz having a spell at Paris St-Germain from 2014 to 2016.

While the deals that took the players back to Chelsea were not specifically referenced, the association was created.

Matic played 35 league games in 2016-17, including 30 in the starting XI. He scored one goal and set up seven.

Only one of those attacking contributions influenced a result, but that was an assist for Chelsea 's first goal in a 2-1 win over Tottenham in November.

Luiz, who was named in the PFA team of the season, started 33 matches and scored one goal - the opener in a 1-1 draw at Liverpool in January.

How Chelsea signed a star team with hidden payments

Chelsea fined but avoid suspended points deduction

Did Chelsea's breaches really impact the title?

Tottenham were relentless at the end of the 2016-17 season, winning 12 of their final 13 matches to finish on 86 points.

Yet Antonio Conte's Chelsea were almost as relentless, winning 11 of their last 13 to take the title with 93 points.

Spurs' tally would have been enough for the title in 2015-16, when Leicester finished on 81.

However, since 1999-2000, when Manchester United were champions on 79 points, 86 points would only have won the title twice, including the two most recent seasons.

Tottenham 's problem in 2016-17 was too many draws at the start of the campaign. Despite an unbeaten 11-game start, only five of those were victories.

Chelsea lost more matches - five to Spurs' four - but secured 30 wins to Tottenham 's 26.

Pochettino might argue that the attacking influence from Willian and Hazard proved the difference, with those two players having attacking contributions in eight different matches which led to points.

Then there is the mere aspect of sporting advantage - how the signings of players like Hazard enabled Chelsea to win trophies, qualify for the Champions League and therefore attract more top talent.

Pochettino feels he should have a Premier League title to his name.

Remember that he managed Chelsea for one season, when he struggled to win over supporters.

Chelsea finished sixth in 2023-24, but neither Pochettino nor the club are likely to look back fondly on that period.

It is different at Tottenham , with the Argentine still adored for his five-year spell in charge from 2014.

As well as finishing as Premier League runners-up, he took the club to the Champions League final in 2018-19.

The 86 points earned in 2016-17 is a club record too.

"Of course I do," said Chris Paouros, co-founder and co-chair of Proud Lilywhites , external and Women of The Lane. , external

"He could tell me the moon was made of halloumi and I'd nod along.

"The Spurs 2016-17 team was the best in the league by most measures: best attack, best defence, fewest defeats, unbeaten at home in the last season of the old White Hart Lane.

"If the playing field was tilted, the least you can do is ask the question."

Paouros knows Spurs will not be handed the title, but said the "rules have to mean something, whoever benefits".

If you get given a title a decade later because of a rule breach, could you celebrate it?

"It would still be something that Spurs fans would celebrate," said Tristan Foot, secretary of the Tottenham Hotspur Supporters' Trust. "A victory over Chelsea , albeit 10 years after the event."

But that sense of injustice is still there for other Premier League clubs.

"It means that to an extent crime does pay in football," Foot said. "And that's the serious underlying part all of this.

"During the transfer window they were signing players that we had no chance of winning, the obvious example being Willian.

"The Premier League has got to be better about imposing sporting sanctions and making sure that its rules actually have teeth."

With all investigations now concluded, it seems unlikely that Pochettino - or anyone else - will get a retrospective trophy parade.

Will clubs get that same feeling when the Manchester City saga is finally over?

articles.title: Mikel Arteta close to signing new contract with Arsenal
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta is believed to be close to finalising a new contract with Premier League champions Arsenal.
articles.body:
The perception of Arsenal 's transfer window varies depending on who you speak to - but there will be no disagreement from anyone at the Emirates Stadium over how crucial their next expected signing will be.

With the market closed until January, the club are now in the process of finalising an agreement with manager Mikel Arteta over his protracted new contract.

Well-placed sources indicate those discussions have moved forward recently amid full confidence from those involved in talks that the Spaniard will renew.

Indeed, Arteta moved unequivocally last month to remove any lingering doubt over his future: "Everybody feels comfortable that the timing of the contract is not going to be an issue because my will certainly is to be here and I'm very happy here.

"My feeling from the club is the same one. That's why everyone is doing things in a very organic way."

Similarly, Arsenal 's chief executive Richard Garlick has said it was merely a "matter of time" before Arteta's new long-term deal was confirmed.

Arteta can expect to become one of the best paid managers in world football once his new contract is signed - Arsenal committed to significantly improving on his current deal, worth £10m a season plus an extra £5m upon Champions League qualification.

Arteta already the longest-serving manager in English football

For Arsenal supporters, the official announcement can't come soon enough, particularly given his current deal now has just nine months left to run.

Since his appointment in December 2019, Arteta has transformed Arsenal from a club that had lost its Champions League status to one that won the Premier League for the first time in 22 years last season.

They are overwhelming favourites to retain their domestic crown and are fancied to win their first-ever Champions League this season.

With that success comes power. Like Arsene Wenger before him, Arteta is categorically the most influential figure, certainly from a football perspective, at the club.

People will say that the manager or head coach should always be the most authoritative figure at any football club - the reality is that is rarely the case.

Arteta's fingerprints are all over the club - and most importantly the squad. Nothing happens from a first-team perspective without his approval.

When Arsenal tried to sign Julian Alvarez and Vinicius Jr last month, it was Arteta who was at the forefront of the club's charm offensive.

With that in mind, the thought of removing Arteta from that dynamic, certainly for Arsenal 's ownership, is the unthinkable.

One day, Spain will come calling - and a return to his homeland may attract Arteta, although he knows he is unlikely to be afforded the same authority at either Real Madrid or Barcelona – clubs that are historically entrenched in internal politics – than he is now.

But at this moment, the attraction for Arteta is with Arsenal .

This is a squad that has flourished under Arteta's tutelage. The average age of the squad (26.2 years) is one of the oldest in the Premier League. It's a group at its peak and primed to build a legacy on.

Beyond the new financial terms and into footballing ambition, Arsenal are buying into Arteta's vision.

The summer arrivals of Bruno Guimaraes and Ezri Konsa were sizeable investments given both turn 30 next year, while the albeit failed pursuits of Vinicius Jr and Alvarez provided Arteta with evidence that the club's American owners are willing to spend heavily on elite talent.

It's the sort of ambition Arteta is understood to have made clear he wanted to see as talks over his contract progressed.

Arteta's six years at the Emirates already makes him the longest-serving manager in the Premier League and EFL by some distance - his new deal will take him closer to a decade in north London.

Yet there appear to be no signs of Arteta taking his foot off the gas.

articles.title: La FIFA desmiente a Marruecos: "La decisión será a su debido tiempo"
articles.standfirst: El máximo dirigente del fútbol marroquí afirmó que el partido más importante de la cita de dentro de cuatro años será en el Gran Estadio Hassan II de Casablanca
articles.summary: El máximo dirigente del fútbol marroquí afirmó que el partido más importante de la cita de dentro de cuatro años será en el Gran Estadio Hassan II de Casablanca
articles.body: La FIFA ha salido al paso de las palabras del máximo dirigente del fútbol marroquí, Fouzi Lekjaa, una de las figuras más populares de la campaña electoral que estrena hoy Marruecos por el Partido Autenticidad y Modernidad (PAM, liberal), y que afirmó que la final del Mundial 2030 se jugará en el Gran Estadio Hassan II de Casablanca, aún en construcción. Según ha podido constatar MARCA de un portavoz de la FIFA, "tal como se comunicó el 5 de agosto de 2026, la FIFA tomará una decisión a su debido tiempo", aseguran. Todo esto incide en la crisis interna en FIFA por su polémico proyecto para vender una participación de los futuros ingresos del Mundial a inversores privados, iniciativa que finalmente abandonó ante la enorme oposición. La pérdida de apoyos de varias federaciones y la posibilidad de que aparezcan candidatos alternativos han puesto en duda su continuidad, y el diario 'The Times' hace un mes ya interpretó su acercamiento a Marruecos también dentro de esa batalla por el poder, al punto que ese pasado 5 de agosto publicó que el presidente de la FIFA había ofrecido la final del Mundial a Marruecos. "Es falso y engañoso afirmar que el presidente de la FIFA haya hecho promesa alguna en relación con la sede de la final de la Copa Mundial de la FIFA 2030. La FIFA tomará una decisión a su debido tiempo", fueron entonces las declaraciones de un portavoz de la organización. Ahora se repiten apenas un mes después con las palabras del ministro. Lekjaa, que también es ministro delegado encargado del Presupuesto y uno de los responsables del auge del fútbol marroquí en los últimos años, hizo estas declaraciones en una reunión electoral. El Mundial 2030 será organizado por España, Portugal y Marruecos. Además, Uruguay, Argentina y Paraguay albergarán los encuentros inaugurales de sus respectivas selecciones como homenaje al centenario de la Copa del Mundo de 1930, celebrada íntegramente en Montevideo. La FIFA aún no ha dado a conocer las sedes de cada país y, por tanto, también se desconoce la que albergará la final.

articles.title: Fabian Hurzeler: Brighton head coach on Europe, ambition and challenging the Premier League establishment
articles.summary: Fabian Hurzeler has made his mark at Brighton, but after two eighth-placed finishes and a summer of change, the 33-year-old believes the club can take another step with a European campaign ahead; Watch Coventry vs Brighton this Sunday live on Sky Sports, kick-off 2pm
articles.body:
"Last season we did it, maybe not through the whole season, but definitely we had a lot of great achievements," he told Sky Sports, with Brighton set to compete in Europe for only the second time in their history.

Beating Manchester City, Chelsea and Liverpool, criticising Arsenal and Mikel Arteta's style , clashing with Pep Guardiola and collecting a string of touchline bans - there has been little doubt about Hurzeler's impact over his two seasons in the Premier League.

His passion in the dugout has become a defining feature of his proactive style, which has delivered consecutive eighth-placed finishes.

It has landed him in trouble, too, but that is nothing new. At St Pauli, he once collected seven yellow cards before February.

"It definitely won't change," he said. "I want to be a winner, I want to win things for Brighton, I want to achieve together with the fans something special."

The Conference League, which begins next month, gives Brighton another opportunity to turn their recent progress into silverware. They watched rivals Crystal Palace lift the trophy in May, but for Hurzeler, the challenge is less about matching them and more about proving Albion can compete on multiple fronts.

"We have high expectations of ourselves. We want to play a season the fans will always remember, but we have to see as a club that we are capable of playing a lot of games in a very successful way," he said.

"We always [talk] of making the next step, growing as a club, and therefore we have to show now that we are capable of being successful and achieving things without losing our style and intensity."

Hurzeler now has the fourth-youngest squad in the Premier League after a busy summer in which 11 players arrived, alongside the departures of established figures including Carlos Baleba, Jan Paul van Hecke, Danny Welbeck and James Milner.

It is a changed squad, but Hurzeler believes his age gives him an advantage in getting the best out of it.

"I want to be myself, I don't want to play a role, and my age definitely helps regarding understanding the players," he said.

"I always say I speak their language and I understand their thoughts, because it wasn't that long ago when I played. I didn't play on their level, but I understand their feelings, their thoughts, maybe their doubts, their fears, what every player has."

That understanding will be important as Brighton integrate another batch of talented young signings, centre-back Luka Vuskovic already proving a smart buy at £50m from Tottenham. Hurzeler trusts the club's recruitment model to deliver again - and his staff to get the best out of them.

He has overseen a victory, a draw and a defeat in their first three Premier League games of this season, having had more big chances (15) and a higher xG (7.4) than any other side while only Arsenal (24) and Man City (26) have faced fewer shots (33).

"It's now our responsibility to really integrate these new players. They are here for a reason, and we proved in the past that we have one of the best recruitment systems in the world, so they have potential and they will show this potential."

Hurzeler was a surprise appointment when he replaced Roberto De Zerbi, but two seasons in he is no longer the unknown quantity he was when he arrived.

The demands of the Premier League have helped shape him, too, from facing the best managers in the world to dealing with the pressure of a long season. But when things go wrong, Hurzeler looks closer to home.

"I can say that I'm a better manager now than I was before, but not only because I reflect on my mistakes; I reflect on my decisions, I reflect on my progress and my development," he said. "I have great staff around me, I have great experts, great support from all of my staff members and I have great support from my team and great personalities."

That approach was tested midway through last season, when Brighton won just once in 13 league games. Hurzeler did not look for someone else to blame.

"I'm not going home and blaming others. If we lose, it's my responsibility, and I reflect on my decisions, I reflect on the training week, so I really try to get better after every game, and that's how I do it."

He says Brighton eventually turned the run around by focusing on what they could control rather than results, maintaining their belief and demanding greater reliability from the players on the pitch.

The lesson was simple, but important for a team trying to challenge the Premier League's established order.

"In the Premier League you need to have reliability, in the Premier League you need to be really good in the small matches," Hurzeler said.

Hurzeler has committed himself to finding that consistency at Brighton, signing a new three-year contract in May. His decision was driven as much by his relationship with the club as by what he believes it can achieve.

"I see my future here, and that's why I extended the contract, because when I started here, it felt like I got integrated into a family," he said. "You don't leave your family, you want to achieve something with the family, you want to make the next step, you want to grow as a club, and therefore I want to be part of it."

He believes that the next step is still within reach.

"I still feel that the journey is not over, I still feel we are in the middle of a journey and we can achieve great things," he said. "I have this belief and now we have to show it."

articles.title: Noah Okafor: Leeds forward rules out playing for Switzerland under Murat Yakin
articles.summary: Leeds United forward Noah Okafor says he will not play for Switzerland again while Murat Yakin remains as head coach.
articles.body:
Leeds United forward Noah Okafor has announced he will not play again for Switzerland under the leadership of Murat Yakin, citing a breakdown in trust with the head coach.

The 26-year-old has earned 26 caps for the Swiss national team since making his debut in 2019 but only featured for 19 minutes at the World Cup, coming off the bench in their last-32 win over Algeria.

In a statement released on his Instagram account on Thursday, Okafor said his decision was unrelated to his lack of game time, instead attributing it to how he feels he has been treated by the current leadership.

"My decision has nothing to do with my playing time," Okafor wrote. "Things happened that hurt me deeply. Trust was broken. Commitments were not kept.

"When I was allowed to play against Algeria, people reacted to minor mistakes far away from our goal in a way that hurt me deeply.

"In the weeks that followed, I thought a lot and decided for myself that I no longer want to play for the national team under the current manager."

The Swiss FA was informed by Okafor on Thursday, with a spokesperson telling Reuters: "We respect his decision and wish him every success with his club."

Leeds manager Daniel Farke has promised to support Okafor, who joined the club from AC Milan for £18m in August 2025, stating "we have a home here for Noah" and backing him to be a "key player" in the Premier League.

"He came to inform me and explained the reasons why, and I appreciate that he spoke with me beforehand and I was well informed," Farke said.

"It's more or less Noah's decision, he has to decide what is best at this stage for his career. All I can say is we have a home here for Noah, where he feels really comfortable, appreciated, and for us he will be a key player.

"What he decides with his international career, with the national team - that's totally up to him. I don't want to get in the way. I think it's more or less for Noah's family to decide what is best."

Switzerland are next in action on 26 September, travelling to North Macedonia for their opening match of the 2026-27 Nations League.

Yakin has been head coach of Switzerland since August 2021.

articles.title: Premier League Christmas fixtures: Seven games scheduled for Boxing Day as festive schedule is announced
articles.summary: The Premier League will stage seven matches on Boxing Day this year - a significant increase on last year.
articles.body:
The Premier League has announced it will stage seven matches on Boxing Day this year after releasing its festive schedule.

Four fixtures will be staged at 15:00 GMT, with further matches played at 12:30, 17:30 and 20:00.

The fixture programme for 26 December, which falls on a Saturday in 2026, is considerably bigger than last year, when one game was held .

Three matches will be played on Sunday, 27 December, while three further rounds of games will be held over a period up to Thursday, 7 January.

A round of evening midweek fixtures will staged on 29-30 December, while Leeds will host Everton (20:00) for the only match on New Year's Day.

The remainder of that round will be held over the weekend of 2-3 January, with the fourth round of games spread across the evenings of 5-7 January.

The Premier League has brought forward the announcement of fixture scheduling over the Christmas and New Year period after consultation with both broadcast partners and the Football Supporters' Association and representatives from club Fan Advisory Boards.

Television scheduling for Premier League fixtures has been announced up to Monday, 2 November, with broadcast selections for the remaining games in November and December to be announced in the weeks commencing 21 September and 19 October respectively.

The Premier League has guaranteed clubs at least a 60-hour break between fixtures over the festive period to address the concerns over a congested festive schedule that follows recent expansions of the European and international calendars.
